spans.s:
Udra is the name of an animal occurring only in the list of sacrificial victims at the aśvamedha given in the Saṃhitās of the yajurveda. According to Mahīdhara it was a crab; but as the commentary on the taittirīya Saṃhitā calls it a watercat, there can be no doubt that it was an otter.
Foot notes taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 5, 20, 1; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 14, 18; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxiv. 37.
On Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, loc. cit.
Loc. cit.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 95, 96; Schrader, Prehistoric Antiquities, 247. Udrin occurs in the baudhāyana śrauta sūtra, ii. 5.
